title: Petrograd Women Workers' Strike on International Women's Day
note: The mass strike and bread demonstrations launched by female textile workers in the Vyborg district of Petrograd on International Women's Day (23 February O.S. / 8 March N.S. 1917), which sparked the citywide general strike and culminated in the collapse of the Romanov monarchy.

title: 1916 Central Asian Revolt (Urkun)
note: Uprising across Russian Turkestan and the Steppe Governorates by Kazakh, Kyrgyz, and Uzbek populations resisting tsarist military conscription decrees in 1916; brutally suppressed by tsarist punitive expeditions, precipitating mass refugee flight across the Tian Shan into China.

title: Execution of the Romanov Imperial Family at Yekaterinburg
note: The extrajudicial midnight shooting of deposed Tsar Nicholas II, Empress Alexandra, their five children, and four attendants in the cellar of the Ipatiev House by Bolshevik Ural Soviet Cheka guards under Yakov Yurovsky as anti-Bolshevik Czech and White troops approached.

title: Anti-Jewish Pogroms in Ukraine during the Russian Civil War
note: Systemic mass violence and massacres targeting Jewish communities across Ukraine and western borderlands during the Civil War, perpetrated primarily by the White Army of Denikin, Ukrainian Directorate forces, and peasant warlord bands, murdering an estimated 50,000 to 100,000 Jewish civilians.

title: First Congress of the Peoples of the East in Baku
note: A landmark assembly convened by the Communist International in Baku in September 1920, gathering nearly 1,900 delegates across Asia and the Middle East (including Turkey, Persia, India, and Central Asia) to proclaim revolutionary anti-colonial solidarity against Western imperialism.
